headline: Pope Leo has lung cancer, the Vatican says
deck: Surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung on Tuesday; he is expected to spend a week in hospital.
standard: Pope Leo XIV, the 71-year-old head of the Catholic Church, has lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer, the Vatican said on Tuesday. Surgeons in Rome removed the lower lobe of his right lung in an operation of about an hour and a half, without complications.
He is expected to spend a week in hospital, and his audiences are cancelled until 20 October. He is due to tour Uruguay, Argentina and Peru for 11 days from 6 November.
Further tests are being carried out to see whether the cancer has spread, an unnamed Vatican source told AFP. It is Leo's first serious illness in 17 months as pope.
short: Pope Leo XIV, the 71-year-old head of the Catholic Church, has lung cancer, the Vatican said on Tuesday after surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is expected to spend a week in hospital.
